title: Week 26 Check-In · The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe
description: This week you read Chapters 4 to 6: Edmund meets the Queen, lies about Narnia, and all four children step through the wardrobe. You practiced keeping verbs in the same tense, the root form (shape), and counting the beats in long school words. Show what you know!

questions.text: Which sentence has a verb tense mistake?
options: Edmund walked into Narnia and felt the cold air.
Edmund walked into Narnia and feels the cold air.
Edmund walks into Narnia and feels the cold air.

questions.text: Is Edmund responsible for his choices in Chapters 4 and 5, or is the enchanted Turkish Delight mostly to blame? Use details to support your opinion.

Model sentence from the book: “The more he ate the more he wanted to eat, and he never asked himself why the Queen should be so inquisitive.” Write your own sentence that starts with “The more…” and shows one thing leading to another.
What did Edmund want, and how did the Queen use that to get what she wanted? Write 1–2 sentences.

passage.title: Reading passage (The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, Chapter 4)
passage.text:
While he was eating the Queen kept asking him questions. At first Edmund tried to remember that it is rude to speak with one’s mouth full, but soon he forgot about this and thought only of trying to shovel down as much Turkish Delight as he could, and the more he ate the more he wanted to eat, and he never asked himself why the Queen should be so inquisitive. She got him to tell her that he had one brother and two sisters, and that one of his sisters had already been in Narnia and had met a Faun there.
— C.S. Lewis, The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, Chapter 4
